Empowerment Elimination, Anti-Corruption and Funds Recovery Committee

Khartoum, Sudan

1 central bank tied to it.

INVESTIGATED, CHARGED OR TRIED ITS OFFICIALS (CENTRAL BANK OF SUDAN (SUDAN))

Source says: Central Bank of Sudan (Sudan). Empowerment Elimination, Anti-Corruption and Funds Recovery Committee pressured, dismissed or prosecuted officials of the Central Bank of Sudan (Sudan). Sudan's transitional government set up a body called the Empowerment Elimination, Anti-Corruption, and Funds Recovery Committee. Radio Dabanga reported on 9 February 2020 that this committee dissolved the board of directors of the Central Bank of Sudan, along with the boards of eleven other banks, over the bank's alleged links to the deposed government of Omar Al Bashir. Nine of the bank's managers were dismissed at the same time. The report names no individual board member and does not set out the evidence the committee relied on. Anti-Corruption Committee dissolves boards of Central Bank of Sudan and 11 other banks (Radio Dabanga)

OTHER TIES: NAMED IN A CASE, PRINTS ITS MONEY, AUDITS OR MANAGES FUNDS (NATIONAL BANK OF SERBIA (SERBIA))

Source says: National Bank of Serbia (Serbia). The National Bank of Serbia vaults, Belgrade holds gold reserves belonging to the National Bank of Serbia (Serbia). The NBS Annual Report 2024 section 'Structure and profitability of FX reserves' lists the components of FX reserves at 31 December 2024 as foreign securities (59.16%), FX funds in accounts abroad (22.04%), gold in NBS vaults (13.26%), foreign cash and SDRs. The whole 48.1-tonne gold holding is placed in the NBS's own vaults; no foreign custodian appears. Storage, not management. National Bank of Serbia, Annual Report 2024
